cases.title: Base rate, loss cost multiplier and ISO loss cost refresh loaded correctly
cases.description: A base rate table (+5%), a loss cost multiplier table (+3%) and a very large ISO loss cost table (14,400 cells, +2.5%) are all refreshed. Everything is loaded exactly as approved.

runs.name: with baseline

must_tests.what: Quote on the filing date using the changed 501 BLD Base Rate Refresh table.
must_tests.expect: The rating worksheet should use the new rates (rate book 2025-V2). Also, the Base Rate Factor for 501 BLD Base Rate Refresh should be 0.7592. It changed by 5.0% in this filing.

must_tests.what: Quote a new business policy effective the day before the filing date.
must_tests.expect: The rating worksheet should use the old rates (rate book 2025-V1).

must_tests.what: Renew a policy with an effective date on or after the filing date.
must_tests.expect: The rating worksheet should use the new rates (rate book 2025-V2).

must_tests.what: Make a mid-term policy change on a policy whose term started before the filing date.
must_tests.setup: A policy that started before 3/15/2027; add a premium-bearing change effective on or after 3/15/2027.
must_tests.expect: The rating worksheet should keep the original rates (rate book of the term inception), not the new ones.

runs.gate: All approved values match PolicyCenter. Ready for QA testing.

summary.scope_check: We also checked tables outside this change against the 'before' export: provided (baseline.xlsx, edition 2025-V1).

probes.what: Table 630 loaded correctly and matched by its number
probes.note: The tool reported 2 problem(s) on a table that was fine.

sample.plain_what: The story says to change 'Deductible Factor', but that table is not in the approved workbook.
'630 Deductible Factor' is in the approved workbook, but the story does not mention it.

gaps.title: Approved tabs whose name has the table number in the middle cannot be matched
gaps.plain: "TAB 614 - Error Cell Factor" and (isolated test) "TAB 701 - Roofing Surcharge" and "Copy of 703 Wind Relativity" are not matched to their PolicyCenter tables, although the rest of the name is identical. Names that start with the number, or carry it at the end or after an underscore ("709 ...", "Theft Device Credit (704)", "702_Sprinkler_Allowance") were matched. A run with such a tab is blocked.
gaps.cause: Table numbers are only recognised at the start of a name or after the word "Table" (mapping/identity.py). Without a number the best possible score is 0.35, below the 0.80 needed for a confident match.
gaps.fix: Accept any standalone number in the tab name that equals a PolicyCenter table number, and let an identical name plus identical key columns count as a match.

gaps.case_title: Two tables with the same name but different numbers
gaps.title: Same table name with different numbers - the story's table number is ignored
gaps.plain: The story says "Table 630 Deductible Factor". PolicyCenter has tables 630 and 631 with that name and the base book has a third, unnumbered one. The tool could not decide which one the story meant, so it reported a correct, approved table as "not in the approved workbook" (a high-severity finding) and failed the run. A second isolated test (a table whose name equals a base-book table name) reproduced it.

observed.plain_what: The story says to change 'Deductible Factor', but that table is not in the approved workbook.
'630 Deductible Factor' is in the approved workbook, but the story does not mention it.

gaps.cause: resolve_jira() scores an unnumbered table with an identical name the same as the table whose number matches (both 1.0). The tie falls inside the required margin, so the story line stays unresolved (mapping/tables.py).
gaps.fix: When a story line carries a table number and exactly one table has that number, prefer it over any name-only match. Treat unnumbered tables as weaker candidates.

gaps.case_title: Scope - bypassed, deprecated and untargeted tables changed
gaps.title: Changing a table the story says "DO NOT LOAD" is not caught when no before-export is supplied
gaps.plain: With a before-export the tool flags it. Without one (the normal case) it says nothing, although the table carries the new filing date and edition. The specification promises a needs-review item here.
gaps.cause: The date-based fallback (OUT_OF_SCOPE_TABLE_DATED) only looks at tables that are not mentioned in the story. Tables the story marks as bypass are skipped, and the strict bypass check needs a before-export.
gaps.fix: Extend the date/edition fallback to tables the story marks as bypass, struck through or removed: if one carries the new filing date or edition, raise a needs-review item (specification section 2, row "Bypassed table modified").

gaps.case_title: Scope - bypassed, deprecated and untargeted tables changed
gaps.title: Updating a struck-through (deprecated) table is not caught when no before-export is supplied
gaps.plain: Same situation as the bypassed table: caught with a before-export, silent without one.
gaps.cause: Same as F7-580b - struck-through tables are treated as bypass and skipped by the date fallback.

gaps.case_title: State mirroring - Arizona values in a California export
gaps.title: A table labelled for the wrong state inside the book goes unnoticed
gaps.plain: In the California book, one table was labelled Arizona. The tool said nothing about it. It only checks the state (and line of business) of the book as a whole, not each table's own label.
gaps.cause: The state/line check compares one book-level value with the story (engines/metadata.py). Isolated test: labelling every table Arizona is caught, labelling about half is caught, labelling a single table is not.
gaps.fix: Compare each table's own state and line-of-business label with the story and raise one finding per table that disagrees.

gaps.title: One unmatched tab produces three separate findings
gaps.plain: An approved tab that cannot be matched is reported as "needs mapping", again as "the story's table is not in the approved workbook" and a third time as "in the workbook but not in the story". The second and third statements are consequences of the first.
gaps.cause: Scope checks run on the unmatched names instead of waiting for the mapping to be resolved.
gaps.fix: Suppress the scope findings for a table that is still waiting for mapping, and mention it once.

gaps.case_title: Same thing written differently, and genuine typos
gaps.title: Limits written 100k / 300k / 1M: one formatting problem becomes 10 findings
gaps.plain: "$300,000" is read correctly (no finding). But "300k" and "1M" are not understood, so every one of the five limits shows up as a missing row and an extra row, 10 high-severity findings for one root cause.

observed.plain_what: Table '571 ILF Limits Short Form' (Limit = 100000) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '571 ILF Limits Short Form' (Limit = 1000000) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '571 ILF Limits Short Form' (Limit = 2000000) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '571 ILF Limits Short Form' (Limit = 300000) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.

gaps.cause: Key text is compared exactly after normalisation. Currency symbols and thousands separators are stripped but k/M shorthand is not.
gaps.fix: Read k/M suffixes in numeric key columns, or roll all unmatched keys of a table into one "keys are written differently" finding with two examples.

gaps.case_title: Same thing written differently, and genuine typos
gaps.title: "Commercial" in the approved file vs code CMP_MONO in PolicyCenter: 20 findings
gaps.plain: The two sides use a label and a code for the same policy type. The tool cannot know they are the same, which is safe, but it reports 10 missing and 10 extra rows instead of one clear message.

observed.plain_what: Table '572 Policy Type Split Matrix' (Coverage = BI, Policy Type = CMP_MONO) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '572 Policy Type Split Matrix' (Coverage = BI, Policy Type = CMP_PKG) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '572 Policy Type Split Matrix' (Coverage = BLD, Policy Type = CMP_MONO) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.
Table '572 Policy Type Split Matrix' (Coverage = BLD, Policy Type = CMP_PKG) is in PolicyCenter but is not in the approved file.

gaps.cause: Row keys differ in every row, so every row is a separate missing/extra pair.
gaps.fix: When none (or nearly none) of a table's keys match, report one finding with examples, and offer a learned value alias ("Commercial = CMP_MONO") like the existing table aliases.

gaps.case_title: Scope - bypassed, deprecated and untargeted tables changed
gaps.title: With a before-export, 52 untouched tables still get a "date matches this filing" review item
gaps.plain: When some tables carry the new date and others the old one, every untouched table with the new date is reported for review (52 findings), even when the before-export proves it did not change. The two real problems are buried among them.
gaps.cause: OUT_OF_SCOPE_TABLE_DATED does not use the baseline comparison when one is available. It is only silent when all tables share one stamp.
gaps.fix: Skip the date check for tables that are identical to the before-export; keep it only for the no-baseline fallback.

gaps.case_title: State mirroring - Arizona values in a California export
gaps.title: Wrong-state values are reported as 85 separate cell findings
gaps.plain: All five mirrored tables are caught, but as 85 individual wrong cells. Nothing says "every row of these tables differs", which is the signature of a whole table copied from another state or edition.
gaps.cause: Cell-level findings are never summarised per table.
gaps.fix: Add one headline per table when most rows differ ("Table 590: 20 of 20 rows differ - possible wrong-state or wrong-edition load") and keep the cell list underneath.

gaps.title: A formula without a saved result is reported twice, and the advice for the second one is wrong
gaps.plain: The cell is reported as "formula with no saved result" and again as "factor cell is blank", with the advice "Enter the approved value". The approved file is where the problem is; the advice reads as if PolicyCenter were wrong.
gaps.cause: The unreadable approved cell is also treated as a blank factor in the comparison.
gaps.fix: Do not run the blank-factor check on a cell already reported as unreadable.

gaps.title: A vague warning duplicates the hidden-sheet finding
gaps.plain: "Something unusual was found in an input file" appears next to the specific "A hidden tab was found" message. The vague one adds nothing; the detail is only in the technical text.
gaps.cause: Input warnings and the hidden-sheet finding are both raised for the same sheet.
gaps.fix: Drop the vague line when a specific finding covers it, or put the specific text in the plain message.

gaps.title: Action words inside a table name are removed from the Jira table name
gaps.plain: "Table 622 Plain Update Table" is read as table 622 named "Plain Table". The number still identifies the table, so nothing went wrong here, but a table whose name consists mainly of an action word could be misread.
gaps.cause: The Jira parser strips action keywords (UPDATE, ADD, REMOVE...) from the whole line, including the table name.
gaps.fix: Strip action words only from the part of the line before the table number or name.

gaps.case_title: Same thing written differently, and genuine typos
gaps.title: >= 100 against Min=100 / Max blank is caught, but the explanation points at the wrong thing
gaps.plain: The tool correctly stops (one finding, not noisy). The message says it could not match the table to PolicyCenter, but the tab name and number match perfectly; the real difference is that one side has a single "Policy Count" column and the other has Min and Max columns.
gaps.cause: Column-set differences are reported with the generic "could not match table" text.
gaps.fix: Say "the columns differ: approved has Policy Count; PolicyCenter has Count Min and Count Max" and mention that ">= N" can be read as Min = N, Max blank.

gaps.case_title: Equivalent ways of writing the same value
gaps.title: Warning about lost leading zeros on protection class codes that never had any
gaps.plain: Protection classes 1 to 10 are stored as numbers in the approved file and as text in PolicyCenter. The tool warns that codes "may have lost leading zeros (for example 0123 became 123)". The values are identical on both sides, so there is nothing to lose. The warning moves a clean run from PASS to PASS_WITH_WARNINGS. The specification does allow this warning when padding cannot be determined, so our expectation of a plain PASS was strict.

observed.plain_what: Some codes in '517 PPC Grade Factor' look like numbers and may have lost leading zeros (for example 0123 became 123).

gaps.cause: A numeric cell in a text-typed key column always triggers the warning when the cell has no zero-padding number format; the export side is not consulted.
gaps.fix: Only warn when the export holds a zero-padded code that matches the approved number once padded. If every code matches as written, stay quiet.
